sasha: Hey — FYI last night's nightly eval has a weird nondeterministic regression on the quantized bring-up for redwood-v1-3b-q4. Some prompt cases flip between good/bad generations across runs and we also saw a handful of per-test timeouts (30s). Not consistent per-prompt, looks run-level.
sasha: Minimal summary: nightly run 2026-03-19 02:12 UTC, job 4821. 3 prompts flagged by quality checks, two of them produce different completions on repeat runs with same seed. I ran the harness twice locally and got different outputs ~40% of the time.
(eval log excerpt)
```
EVAL: prompt_id=chat-512 sample_seed=42 model=redwood-v1-3b-q4
expected: "...the user should do X"
observed run A: "...the user should do X"
observed run B: "...the user should not do X"
TIMEOUT: prompt_id=qa-210 (30s)
```
sasha: This started after the eval-harness worker-pool change in the PR merged yesterday (ref: a1b2c3d). cc @mike @rachel

mike: thanks. sounds like classic RNG/worker forking footgun after the pool refactor. Did we switch to fork-based workers anywhere? IIRC the refactor uses multiprocessing.Pool with default on linux (fork).

sasha: yeah the refactor created a long-lived worker pool at harness startup. We initialize seeds at process start in the parent, not per worker. oops.

eval-bot: CI: nightly-evals/4821 finished — 3 quality alert(s), 12 timed out(s). Link: https://ci.redwood.internal/4821 :warning:

rachel: also saw a few OOMs on the quantized path when reproducing locally with multiple workers. mmap flags and per-worker memory reservation might differ after fork. worth checking.

mike: repro plan: run the harness single-threaded (no worker pool) and run it with a worker pool but set deterministic seeding per-worker. Two quick checks:
1) reproduce without parallel: `./run_eval.sh --prompts=nightly --model=redwood-v1-3b-q4 --no-parallel --seed 42`
2) reproduce with explicit worker init: (example)
```
from multiprocessing import Pool

def init_worker(seed):
    import os, random, numpy as np, torch
    random.seed(seed + os.getpid())
    np.random.seed(seed + os.getpid())
    torch.manual_seed(seed + os.getpid())

with Pool(4, initializer=init_worker, initargs=(42,)) as p:
    p.map(run_prompt, prompt_list)
```

julian: another fix is to set the multiprocessing start method to 'spawn' or explicitly reseed in worker entrypoint. Fork preserves RNG state from parent which causes correlated/duplicated streams.

sasha: trying mike's single-thread repro now. also will add per-worker reseed in harness. quick test: `python -c "import random,os
print(random.random()); os.fork(); print(random.random())"` shows identical sequences with fork.

rachel: for the mmap/OOMs, check `mmap.MAP_SHARED` usage in quantizer and whether file descriptors are duplicated across forks. If a worker maps same file descriptor multiple times it can blow memory accounting.

mike: related quick mitigation: call `torch.set_num_threads(1)` and `numpy.random.seed()` inside worker initializer to avoid unexpected thread-level nondeterminism. Also set `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` for CPU ops where available (note: may change perf).

sasha: local single-thread run: reproduces bad generation 0/5 (no flip). worker-pool run with current harness: reproduces flip 3/5. After adding per-worker reseed (seed + pid) flip reduced to 0/5 in my quick loop.

julian: sounds like we should patch harness to reseed on worker start + include start_method='spawn' guard for CI. Also add a small randomized smoke test that runs a few prompts under 3 different seeds and fails CI if outputs diverge unexpectedly.

mike: filed GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/689 — implements worker reseed, sets spawn on linux CI, and adds smoke test. @sasha can you add a quantized mmap check in the PR? @rachel please eyeball for OOM risk.

sasha: yep will add mmap safety checks and attach failing job logs to the PR. I'll also add the `--no-parallel` repro to the runbook.

rachel: I'll run stress with 8 workers on a small quantized model to see if there are any fd/mmap dup issues and post results here.

sasha: action items: (1) patch harness reseed (PR opened), (2) add `--no-parallel` repro to runbook, (3) rachel to investigate mmap/OOM, (4) add CI smoke test. Marking as high priority for Dedicated bring-up tomorrow. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks. shout if anything else. :eyes:
